bio: Old Great Dividing Range pass in Main Range National Park, with a short walk to the Governors Chair lookout.
The original road over the Great Dividing Range west of Brisbane, now a base for campers and bushwalkers.
Gondwana Rainforests mountain pass near Brisbane, with a 300 m return walk to a cliff-edge lookout.
scenic-rim-7.notes: Hours estimated from the ~15 min lookout walk. Variant 3 'near Brisbane' is loose (about 100 km). Governors Chair walk length comes from a search snippet of the blocked QPWS page; check before shipping.

bio: Scenic Rim reservoir with a designated swimming area, popular for waterskiing and jetskiing.
Lake on Reynolds Creek with a swimming area at A G Muller Park and dam-wall access to Mount Edwards.
Swim, waterski or fish on the Moogerah Dam lake, where fishing needs a stocked impoundment permit.
Fifteen scuttled ships off Tangalooma form a reef for snorkelling with turtles, wobbegongs and fish.
Artificial reef of 15 scuttled vessels north of Tangalooma Island Resort, with 200+ fish species.
Sunken ship reef a short way north of Tangalooma, reached by resort snorkel tour or private boat.
moreton-island-1.notes: Hours estimated (a snorkel session). Variant 3 'a short way north' paraphrases 'north of the resort'. Wiki field is a section anchor of the Tangalooma article, so the lead image may be the resort's, not the wrecks'.

bio: Queensland's oldest lighthouse, a sandstone tower with two red bands, viewed from the Cape Moreton headland.
Queensland's oldest lighthouse marks the northern entrance to Moreton Bay from the island's northeast tip.
Heritage-listed lighthouse at Moreton Island's northeast tip, closed to the public but seen from outside.
moreton-island-3.notes: The lighthouse is closed to the public per the research, so no variant invites entry. Whether the old quarters museum is open is unverified, so it is left out. Hours estimated for a headland stop.

bio: Heritage-listed WWII battery at Cowan Cowan, closed by 1960, with much of it since removed.
WWII fort at Cowan Cowan on Moreton Island, listed on the Queensland Heritage Register in 2007.
moreton-island-6.notes: MARGINAL: the only source found is Wikipedia. It says much of the fort is removed or lost into the residential township, and no visitor source or public-access detail was found, so it may fail COVERAGE bar 2. Suggest sending it to review. Hours estimated.

bio: Short clifftop boardwalk at Point Lookout for spotting dolphins, turtles, manta rays and humpback whales.
Point Lookout clifftop walk with humpback whales May to October and manta rays November to February.
Restored clifftop boardwalk at Point Lookout, reopened in 2021 after storm damage, for sea-life spotting.
north-stradbroke-island-2.notes: Wildlife and season claims come from a council search summary, and the council page returned 404 on fetch, so they are unverified. The reopening date comes from a local news headline. No Wikipedia article, so the photo needs checking. Hours estimated.

bio: Minjerribah national park containing Kaboora (Blue Lake), with two sections open to visitors.
North Stradbroke Island national park that contains the former Blue Lake National Park.
